children: British finance minister John Healey on Wednesday reversed plans to slash the amount that people can invest in tax-free cash savings accounts, in a move expected to be welcomed by consumer groups and banks.
In his maiden budget, Healey told parliament that the annual, tax-free limit for cash investments in an Individual Savings Account (ISA) would remain at £20,000 ($26,570) for all investors.

Former finance minister Rachel Reeves had planned to cut the annual cash ISA limit to £12,000 for under-65s from next year in an effort to funnel more funds into Britain's stock market and drive economic growth.
The move by Healey is a boon for banks and building societies, because ISA investments are stickier and can help fund mortgage lending.
